title: Duchy of Modena and Reggio
capsule: The Duchy of Modena and Reggio was an Italian principality ruled by the House of Austria-Este, restored at the Congress of Vienna in 1815 after the Napoleonic interlude and governed first by Francis IV (1815–1846) and then by Francis V (1846–1859). Francis IV crushed the 1831 liberal uprising with Austrian assistance and executed the revolutionary leader Ciro Menotti; Francis V similarly quelled the 1848 revolution before being driven out permanently following Piedmont's victory at the Battle of Magenta (June 1859). In December 1859 Modena merged with Tuscany and Parma as the United Provinces of Central Italy, which was annexed to the Kingdom of Sardinia in March 1860, contributing to the proclamation of the Kingdom of Italy in 1861. The duchy thus ended not by conquest but by plebiscite, as the Austrian-Este line refused compromise with Italian nationalism.
